items.title: The line every monthly report is missing
items.caption:
If you send clients a monthly report, read this line: "Changes made: 14."

The client's next question is always the same. Did they work?

Most reports stop at activity. Adspenta, the marketing tool I'm building for agencies, checks every client's Meta and Google ads and measures each change it sends at day 7 and day 14, against that account's own baseline. So the report can finally say which change actually helped.

items.title: The column clients actually read
items.caption:
Every agency report I've seen has a column for what changed. Almost none have a column for whether it worked.

That missing column is the one clients read first.

Adspenta keeps it. Each change it sends is measured at 7 and 14 days, with one of four honest answers: improved, worse, no change, or not enough data. "Worse" included. That's the point.

Would you show a client a "worse"?

(Short video, AI voice, example data.)

items.title: Applied means nothing
items.caption:
"Applied" is the most reassuring word in ad software, and it tells you almost nothing.

It means the tool sent the change. It doesn't mean the platform shows the new value, and it doesn't mean the change worked.

So Adspenta reads every change it sends back from Meta or Google before it calls it confirmed. Then at day 7 and day 14 it checks the results.

When your tool says "applied", how do you know it landed?

(Short video, AI voice, example data.)
